summary: Sean Payton's return to play-calling turned Denver run-first (29 runs to 28 passes in Week 5), shrinking the Broncos' passing volume ahead of Thursday's Seattle visit, while Denver's secondary is thin with Surtain and Hufanga not practicing. Midweek college games had no posted player props.

NFL|00-0034348|rec.note: Payton's return to play-calling cut Denver to 27 pass attempts, and Sutton drew only 3 targets on 81% of snaps. Seattle's stingy pass defense and possible rain should keep his volume low.

detail.availability: Sutton is not on either estimated injury report this week.
detail.role: With Pat Bryant on IR, Sutton played 50 snaps (81%) in Week 5 but caught 2 of 3 targets. Troy Franklin took most of Bryant's work, so more snaps did not bring Sutton more looks.
detail.matchup: Seattle's defense ranks 2nd in EPA per play and allows about 5.5 yards per pass attempt, and fantasy analysts list Seattle among the defenses that give up the least to receivers.
detail.script: Payton is building the offense around the run, with 29 runs to 28 dropbacks in his first game calling plays, and the total has fallen to about 41.5, both of which point to low pass volume.
detail.conditions: Early forecasts show a chance of showers and gusty wind at Mile High on Thursday night, on a short week for both teams.
detail.market: Kalshi has the over at 41%, so the under at about 59% already clears the 52.4% break-even. The lean is mostly priced in, and the edge is modest.
detail.experts: DraftSharks calls Sutton a hard-to-trust WR4 while Denver's run-pass split holds. One props preview prefers his receptions to his yardage but posts no line.

NFL|00-0039732|car.note: Payton is reworking the run game around Nix, and Seattle's pressure may force scrambles, but no source gives Week 5 designed-run usage. Nothing beyond the stats.

detail.role: Nix played every snap in Week 5. Payton says the offense needs a working run game, and Denver ran it 29 times, but no source broke out Nix's own carries.
detail.script: As a roughly 3-point home underdog in a low-total game, Denver keeps a balanced script, which neither adds to nor cuts Nix's scramble chances.
detail.market: Kalshi has the over at 58%, so the market already prices in his rushing floor.

NFL|00-0031492|kpts.note: Seattle is a road favorite of about 3 with an implied total near 22, but rain and wind could cut either way on kicks. There is no concrete news.

detail.script: The spread has moved from Seattle -1.5 to -3 while the total fell from 43 to about 41.5, implying around 22 Seattle points. Facing a Denver defense that blitzes heavily, some drives may stall into field-goal range.
detail.conditions: Altitude helps distance, but early forecasts include showers and gusty wind, which make longer attempts riskier.

NFL|00-0034869|ryd.note: Darnold has taken 8 sacks in two games, and Denver blitzes heavily, which can create scrambles, but there is no concrete usage news. The market sits near a coin flip.

detail.availability: Darnold is not on the injury report. Backup Drew Lock was limited with a right forearm injury.
detail.matchup: Denver had five sacks against Herbert in Week 5 and blitzes heavily, so Darnold may face pressure that ends in scrambles or sacks.
detail.market: Kalshi has the over at 49.5%, below the 52.4% break-even, with nothing to push it higher.

NFL|00-0040648|rec.note: Horton played only 9 to 11 snaps with no targets in Week 5 as Seattle leaned on multi-tight-end sets; Smith-Njigba's ankle could open snaps for him, so the under is a mild lean only.

detail.availability: Horton is not on the Week 6 injury report and was active in Week 5. The packet's missed-last flag reflects a game with no catches, not an absence.
detail.role: Seattle's Week 5 snaps went to Smith-Njigba (84%), Kupp (81%) and Shaheed (46%), with Horton at 17% and heavy use of tight ends Saubert and Arroyo. RotoWire says Horton needs an injury ahead of him to get meaningful targets.
detail.matchup: Denver's secondary is depleted, but Smith-Njigba and Kupp are the receivers in line to benefit.
detail.market: Kalshi has the over at 58%, which looks high for a fourth receiver at about 15% of snaps. If Smith-Njigba's ankle flares up, Horton's snaps would grow, so recheck his status Thursday.

NFL|00-0039732|pyd.note: Under Payton's play-calling, Nix threw for 123 yards on a season-low 27 attempts. He now faces Seattle's 2nd-ranked EPA defense with a falling total and possible rain.

detail.role: Denver went 29 runs to 28 passes in Payton's first game calling plays, and Dobbins regained the lead-back role.
detail.matchup: Seattle ranks 2nd in defensive EPA per play and allows about 5.5 yards per pass. Nix has averaged under 6.0 yards per attempt in four of five games.
detail.script: The total has dropped from 43 to about 41.5, and previews expect a low-scoring, run-first game from Denver.
detail.market: Kalshi has the over at 49.2%. One props preview sets 209.5 as its dividing line and says to start on the under at 210.5 or above, so the packet's 204.5 is near that threshold.
detail.experts: Covers and SI both lean on Denver's weak passing efficiency when picking the under and Seattle respectively. Passing-yards calls have been this app's weakest category, so the adjustment stays mild.

NFL|00-0036158|car.note: In Payton's first game back calling plays, Dobbins took 18 of Denver's 28 to 29 runs and reclaimed lead-back snaps from Harvey. Payton has made the run game the offense's base. He is off Denver's injury report.

detail.role: Dobbins played 52% of snaps to Harvey's 37% in Week 5 and had 18 carries for 68 yards and a TD, reversing Week 4, when Harvey out-snapped him.
detail.script: Payton says the offense needs a working run game, and a roughly 3-point spread with a low total keeps Denver able to stay balanced.
detail.market: Kalshi has the carries over at 51.5%, just under break-even. The packet's line of 13.5 sits well below his Week 5 workload.
detail.experts: One props preview lists Dobbins' rushing yards as an over at 57.5 or lower.

NFL|00-0038543|recyd.note: Smith-Njigba was limited with an ankle injury, but Denver may be without Surtain and Hufanga, with Moss uncertain. The matchup helps if he is healthy. Check Thursday's status.

detail.availability: He was estimated as limited (ankle) on Monday's report. He finished Sunday's game and played 84% of snaps.
detail.matchup: Surtain and Hufanga did not practice Monday, and Moss was limited. Denver's backup corners Abrams-Draine and Barron played every snap in Week 5.
detail.script: Darnold has thrown for 168 and 195 yards in his last two games, and the total is falling, which caps the passing ceiling.
detail.experts: SI calls him the player to watch against Denver's injured corners. One props preview leans over only at 74.5 or lower and would pass or look at the under at 84.5 or higher.

NFL-SEA-at-DEN-1016.summary: Sean Payton took back Denver's play-calling in Week 5 and ran a near 50/50 run-pass split: Nix threw a season-low 27 passes for 123 yards, and Dobbins got 18 carries. Seattle is about a 3-point road favorite. The total has fallen from about 43 to 41.5 or lower, with rain and wind possible. Denver's secondary is thin: Surtain and Hufanga did not practice, and Moss was limited. Smith-Njigba (ankle) was limited but played 84% of snaps last week.

The total rose from 53.5 to 54.5 and the Rams are about -3 at home indoors.

best.why: No over on this short slate was fully confirmed by the fact-check, so the Best bet is an under.
